what: Hovering a button or link draws two highlighter strokes. The upper stroke goes left to right in .16s power4.out, and the lower stroke goes right to left .048s later. Each stroke is an SVG line (thickness height/2×1.42, slightly tilted) with a segment shown by gradient stops, so the faster the ends, the fainter they are (motion between frames ×2.2, max .3). Only the letters the stroke head has passed switch to the inverted color (upper half and lower half use separate clip-path polygons, including the length where the stroke extends beyond the element, to track progress). On release, both strokes retract from the start point in .136s (the second .054s later). Strokes already drawn are not drawn again. Keyboard focus works the same way.

options.dur: Time for a single stroke to be drawn (s), default .16
options.lag: Share by which the second stroke is delayed (dur multiplier), default .3
options.look: accent: Text color on accent stroke, on accent (the original white pill button has a green stroke with white text)
options.--fx-mk-ink · --fx-mk-on: Stroke color · inverted text color (via style) — default text color stroke · background color text
options.fx:mark: Send to an element to turn it on (detail false turns it off) — for switching on things the hand does not touch directly, like a cursor label

note: Strokes poke out 7~12px beyond the element (based on 48px height, shrinking down to .45x for short elements) and the SVG is 18px wider on every side — don’t let the parent clip it with overflow. The text cover re-clones its children on every hover, so it still fits when the text changes.
